rationale: Normative framing of how a taxonomy should be built.
The survey proposes its own triaxial framework; framing, not a factual claim.
Definitional description of gray-box adversaries.
Asserts specific gray-box neutralization attacks (overconfidence exploitation, representation poisoning) as established, with no source.
States as settled that many decoders have a critical flaw from unverified logit assumptions.
Claims black-box attacks exploit 'radioactive transfer'; the cited black-box attack [28] uses query-based stealing, not radioactivity.
An O(n) vs O(1)-queries asymmetry is asserted as a result; no known source establishes this complexity statement.
Generic warning about weak evaluations.
Superlative 'most empirically pervasive' threat vector stated without evidence.
Maps attack classes onto the survey's own taxonomy.
Claims all output attacks converge on one fragility, making detection 'inherently asymmetric', as settled.
'Zero marginal cost' for output-space adversaries is an unsupported absolute.
Broad, commonly held statement linking scrubbing to the quality-robustness trade-off.
Framing sentence introducing lexical-substitution attacks.
Rhetorical framing of parameter/behavior-space attacks.
Broad contrast between text-level and model-level attacks.
Continues the previous paragraph's attacks but says they need no weight access, although fine-tuning/pruning attacks just described require weights.
The survey's own gap statement.
Radioactivity is presented as a defense against unauthorized distillation in the literature (e.g., [74]); broadly accurate.
Framing that links attacks to an asymmetry argued earlier.
Generic description of distillation-based watermark learning; broadly consistent with the literature.
Introduces pre-distillation paraphrasing (as in [74]); broad statement.
Describes the idea of sanitizing teacher outputs before training.
Concluding framing of the subsection.
Framing of systemic attack surfaces.
Asserts trade-offs 'cannot be resolved' within siloed design as settled.
A no-go result between watermark strength and speculative sampling efficiency exists in the literature (Hu et al. 2024), but it is uncited here.
Specific numbers (42-68% latency penalty at >95% survival, OPT-1.3B/LLaMA-7B) with no source; cannot be verified and may be fabricated.
Guard attenuation/amplification under watermarking is reported in published work on watermarking degrading alignment; uncited here.
Concluding framing calling for co-verification.
Future-direction proposals by the survey.
Claims fingerprinting evaluations are longitudinally blind, though several cited fingerprints test fine-tuning persistence.
Recommendations for benchmarks.
Meta sentence announcing what the conclusion does.
The survey's own formal hypothesis-testing framing of detectability.
